title: Complete EFX for four additive goods agents
statement: For four agents and every finite set M of indivisible goods with nonnegative additive values v_i, does there exist a complete partition X of M such that v_i(X_i)≥v_i(X_j\{g}) for all agents i,j and every g∈X_j? The deletion quantifier includes goods of zero value to i (EFX0).
source_locator: Alkassar et al., Introduction and Theorem 1; He and Tao, Section 6.
status_basis: The August 2026 source still reports the unrestricted four-agent question as open while proving m≤9. Targeted later searches found no general resolution; the suggested m=10 pilot has not received a separate exhaustive novelty check.
plain_summary: Can four people always divide indivisible goods so that removing any one item from someone else's share eliminates envy? A finite number of goods still leaves infinitely many possible valuations.
assumptions: Four agents; a finite good set; nonnegative additive values, with zeros and ties allowed.
Every good belongs to exactly one bundle. Empty bundles are allowed.
Comparisons use the potentially envious agent's valuation of both bundles. EFX0 quantifies over every removed good, including goods that agent values at zero.
scope: The literature question allows arbitrary m. A proposed first milestone uses m=10 and one explicitly specified rational polytope of normalized valuation matrices. This restriction is curator-designed and awaits assessment; it is not a separately verified open case.
target: Seek an existence argument for the full question or a rigorously certified counterexample. A first bounded milestone is an exact EFX0 cover for one stated continuous valuation region, or a concrete counterexample that survives exhaustive allocation checking.
success_criteria: Write the region R as explicit rational linear inequalities in the 40 values before search; explain nonemptiness and any row normalization or symmetry reduction.
For a positive regional result, give a finite menu of complete allocations and an exact proof that every v∈R admits at least one menu allocation satisfying all EFX0 inequalities.
For a negative result, give exact rational valuations and a checkable reason every one of the 4^10 complete allocations fails EFX0.
State uncovered regions and preserve ties and zero values. A regional certificate alone does not settle all ten-good instances or the all-m question.
known_results: SRC-MODEL-201 reports the m≤9 theorem. Its continuous-domain encoding supplies a relevant method; it does not solve unrestricted m.
SRC-MODEL-202 distinguishes additive goods, still open, from chore nonexistence and nonadditive goods counterexamples.
prerequisites: Additive fair division and the distinction between EFX, EFX0, EF1 and partial allocation.
Linear real arithmetic, exact certificates and coverage proofs for a finite union of regions.
Symmetry reductions that preserve one common labeling of goods across all agents.
significance: The four-agent case is a small-agent boundary of exact fair division. A new regional argument could expose reusable structure, but a collection of successful sampled allocations is not an existence theorem.

relations.explanation: Restricting the value alphabet is another route into additive-goods EFX; the unrestricted four-agent and arbitrary-agent three-value questions do not imply one another directly.

requirements.experiment: None for the mathematical existence task. Whether people accept EFX as fair is an empirical question outside this target.
requirements.data: Only explicitly recorded valuation constraints and any future exact candidate matrix; no preference survey is required.
requirements.compute: First-pilot policy: one region, at most 128 menu allocations, one CPU-hour and 8 GiB memory, then stop with an unresolved region if necessary. These are proposed resource caps, not measured requirements or a promise of completion. The complete allocation space at m=10 has 4^10=1,048,576 assignments; exhaustive region coverage may require much more.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Finite indivisibility, additivity, nonnegative values, complete assignment and EFX0 deletion semantics.

ai_assessment.rationale: Exact linear constraints let AI propose regions and allocation menus while a separate checker tests each claim. A specialist must first judge whether the chosen region adds anything to known reductions.

clarity.reason: The allocation and inequality quantifiers are explicit.

decomposability.reason: Encoding, region selection, allocation generation and certificate checking can be separated.

methods.reason: A recent bounded existence proof supplies a concrete continuous-region method.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Linear-real formulas support symbolic reasoning and solver-guided search.

checkability.reason: A finite certificate is possible, but covering continuous regions and validating the encoding require care.

expertise.reason: Fair-division and computer-assisted-proof expertise are needed.

significance.reason: The full target is a central small-agent existence case.

verification_difficulty.reason: All valuations in the claimed region must be covered, including boundary faces.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: Novelty of any chosen ten-good subregion is unverified. Solver difficulty and generalization from local structure are unknown.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI able to manipulate exact formulas, generate auditable code and explain mathematical assumptions.

methods: Exact linear-real encoding of allocation failures.
Counterexample-guided allocation-menu generation on a declared rational polytope.
Proof-carrying region subdivision, with independently checked branch coverage.
obstacles: A finite grid of values cannot prove a statement over real valuations.
Positive results can become vacuous if the selected region only contains a previously solved special class.
Symmetry choices and discarded allocation clauses can silently remove hard boundary cases.

steps: Implement a small independent allocation checker from the displayed EFX0 inequalities, without sharing the search encoder.
For each menu allocation, reconstruct its inequalities directly from bundle membership.
Require an exact checkable proof of unsatisfiability for region-and-failure formulas; cross-checking two solvers is corroboration, not a substitute for an audited encoding.
For a putative counterexample, verify exact nonnegativity and enumerate all complete allocations independently, retaining a violated comparison for each.
Have a fair-division researcher review regional coverage and compare the resulting lemma with existing existence theorems.
validation.human_review_difficulty: High for a universal regional proof: the certificate checker, encoding and region cover all matter. A small concrete allocation is easy to check but does not prove existence for other values.
validation.statement_alignment: Removing a good from the envied bundle is essential; every good is quantified, including zero values. Unallocated goods and approximate inequalities change the target.

known_attempts: Alkassar, Fouz and Mehlhorn (2026) provide a computer-assisted proof through nine goods; their package is an external public record, not a project attempt.
unresolved_checks: Assess the novelty and usefulness of a proposed ten-good region before running it.
Independently inspect the recent m≤9 certificate and any later version before relying on its detailed reductions.
Refresh the all-m four-agent status before any claimed solution.

epistemic_layers.formal_validity: The target is a theorem about idealized additive preferences. Only an aligned proof or exact counterexample supports a mathematical conclusion.
epistemic_layers.empirical_support: No claim about measured human preferences, fairness judgments or implementation outcomes follows from the theorem.

attribution.citation: Alkassar, Fouz and Mehlhorn (2026), arXiv:2608.08590v1; He and Tao (2026), arXiv:2606.08872v1, Section 6. These sources document the target and recent boundary results; the ten-good regional milestone is curator-proposed.
